verdict.rationale: Obsidian's core Bases plugin creates database-like views of notes, letting you view, edit, sort, and filter files by their properties, with a documented Kanban (board) view grouped by a property. Community users confirm it works in practice as a fast, roughly 90% replacement for Dataview. However, the pack does not explicitly document table or list view types or the depth of property querying, and one user notes it is not yet as comprehensive as Dataview. missing for 10: explicit first-party documentation of table and list view types, documentation of the query/filter expressiveness over properties (operators, formulas), evidence that views update live as notes change.

support.subject: As a power-user, I can query my notes by their structured properties and render live database-style views (tables, boards, lists) from those queries

citations.quote: Bases is a core plugin that lets you create database-like views of your notes.
Using a base you can view, edit, sort, and filter files and their properties.
Kanban - Display files as cards organized into columns based on a grouped property.
it's about a 90% replacement and a ton faster and more responsive
